text.p: Italian cash bonds closed down but futures put in a more resilient performance, ending around 20 basis points higher on the day, just short of the recent record peak on the December contract.

"There was some small profit-taking but once it came back to positive ground, technical buying set in," one broker in London said, noting Italian bond futures had managed to keep their head above water even when Bunds dropped back.
The lira cruised to its highest levels on the mark since late June 1994, trading at 982.10 per mark, with unconfirmed talk the Bank of Italy had been in braking its climb.

The broker at the U.S. house said however that doubts were circulating about thorny economic issues in Italy, with Il Sole daily reporting at the weekend the budget deficit for this year was likely to be 140 trillion lire as opposed to the 130 trillion indicated previously by government officials.
"There seem to be a few chinks in the Btps' armour longer term but for now they're riding on the coattails of other markets, which look positive till the end of the year," he said.
At home, the budget bill's progress through the upper house is in focus this week, while final CPI data for November is due Thursday. --Charlotte Cooper, Milan bureau +392 66129507
